The device's own answer (rule 1): a 16-bit float texel's NaN through a `half` `read()` of a read-access texture. Metal hands back the texel's own code (0x7c01 at the first differing element); lavapipe's fetch drops the payload, answering the quiet NaN of its sign (0x7e00). Notes `half-texel-conversion` and `native-half-conversion`. This site answers what read-through-sample answers, and the old runtime on this venue answers it otherwise: both runtimes read each slot with the same ops (`OpImageFetch` of a sampled float image, then `OpFConvert` to `half`), the old one through a set-0 binding per slot and this one through set 1's sampled-texture array at the slot's resource ID, and lavapipe's fetch answers a NaN by descriptor: the old runtime's own two bindings of this one texture answer differently in one dispatch (R16Float: 0x7e00 at read-through-sample and 0x7e01 at read; the ops read from Mesa's SPIR-V dump of both runtimes' modules).
